_readme: Editable conversational-workload scenarios per ENROLLED PATIENT PER MONTH. Every value is an assumption [A] unless the 'basis' says [demo] (measured in the synthetic replay, which is scripted and not evidence of real behavior). Edit numbers here and re-run: python3 costs/workload_scenarios.py

baseline_short_classification.description: The v0.1/v0.2 assumption set: short intent classification, one call per inbound, template replies. Kept for continuity; it does NOT price a longitudinal conversation.

low.description: Quiet cohort: most patients ignore or answer once; short threads.

medium.description: Engaged cohort: 2-4 exchanges per patient, some corrections and re-plans; longer context as threads grow.

high.description: Chatty cohort with caregivers, corrections, cost and clinical questions; long threads; strong-model fallback common.

fixed_operational.note: [A] dashboard review, feed check, queue triage not tied to a specific escalation

development_agent_costs.note: [A] Cost of the coding assistants used to build and maintain the software, NOT patient-service inference. Claude Code and Codex were used on subscriptions during rounds one and two; token totals were not metered here. Enter a monthly figure once the subscription/API mix is known.

self_hosted_scenario.note: ONE scenario, not a statement about open-weight models in general: DeepSeek-V4-Flash on 2x rented H200 (RunPod Secure $4.59/GPU-hr read 2026-09-13) running 24/7, plus 0.25 FTE MLOps. Hardware fit (~170 GB weights, derived not measured), utilization (assumed 500 tok/s capacity, not benchmarked), 24/7 serving (a design choice) and BAA availability (not checked) are all assumptions.
